classification.difficultyReason: Sketch rotations of the basic parabola, including an oblique axis of symmetry.

content.prompt: Consider the basic parabola $y=x^2$. Draw a sketch of the parabola if it is:

children.label: a
children.prompt: rotated about the origin through $135^\circ$ clockwise

answer.short: Vertex $(0,0)$; axis of symmetry $y=-x$; opens towards the lower right.
answer.worked: Rotate the vertex and axis of symmetry through $135^\circ$ clockwise. The vertex remains $(0,0)$ and the positive $y$-axis becomes the ray towards the lower right on $y=-x$. The parabola crosses the axes again at $(\sqrt2,0)$ and $(0,-\sqrt2)$.

spec.description: Complete solution sketch of the basic parabola rotated clockwise through 135 degrees, with the vertex, intercepts and dashed symmetry axis.
spec.mathematics: Parametric curve x=(t²−t)/√2, y=−(t²+t)/√2; vertex (0,0); axis y=−x; intercepts (√2,0) and (0,−√2).

children.label: b
children.prompt: rotated about the origin through $90^\circ$ anticlockwise

answer.worked: A $90^\circ$ anticlockwise rotation sends $(p,p^2)$ to $(-p^2,p)$. Thus the rotated parabola has equation $x=-y^2$, vertex $(0,0)$ and axis of symmetry $y=0$.

spec.description: Complete solution sketch of the left-opening parabola, with coordinate axes and vertex.
spec.mathematics: x=−y²; vertex (0,0); axis of symmetry y=0.
